summary_paragraph: The patient, a man with a history of type 1 diabetes, hypertension, and end-stage renal disease, was admitted for initiation of hemodialysis due to worsening kidney function and a non-maturing AV fistula. A tunneled hemodialysis catheter was successfully placed in the right internal jugular vein on the day of admission. He underwent his first hemodialysis session the following day and tolerated it well, with subsequent sessions showing improvement in fluid and electrolyte balance. Anemia was managed with initiation of Epogen during dialysis, and diabetes remained well-controlled on his prior insulin regimen. Blood pressure medications were adjusted at discharge, with doxazosin reduced to 2mg daily due to improved fluid status. The patient was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue outpatient dialysis through the catheter while awaiting fistula maturation.
problems: Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type I [juvenile type], not stated as uncontrolled
